newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sells more wheat to Iran - AWB.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sells more wheat to Iran - AWB.

text.p: Iran has become Australia's biggest wheat customer with the sale of 1.5 million tonnes during the past week, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said.
AWB chairman Trevor Flugge said the sale added to the one million tonnes already sold to Iran late last year to bring total 1996/97 sales to 2.5 million tonnes.
"The deal further cements our relationship with Iran with whom we've had a long established trading history," Flugge said.
Flugge led an AWB delegation to Iran last week and met Iran's Government Trading Corporation, government officials and ministers.
"The current contracts provide shipment until June this year and we expect more business opportunities for shipment during 1997," Flugge said in a statement.
Flugge said the latest sale to Iran added to the very good start to the AWB's export programme which has alrady seen record shipments in December.
"As well as breaking shipping records, we are also selling record tonnages of wheat for this stage of our marketing programme," he said.
"We have sold more than 50 percent of our projected export commitments so far," Flugge said.
"In light of the latest estimate of the very large crop, the sales to Iran and other customers put in a strong position to maximise export sales opportunities this year," he said.
Australia has also concluded sales to a range of non-traditional buyers this year including India, Sudan, Nigeria and other customers in eastern Africa and South America.
Flugge said the high level of wheat sales were the result of an aggressive marketing strategy and targeted customer and technical servicing.
"Such is the success that our January-February shipping programme is full," he said.
"Logistically, we simply cannot ship any more wheat than we're doing at the moment," he said.
The AWB has forecast a wheat crop of 21.5 million tonnes but other estimates go as high as 24 million tonnes.
